items.title: Sheryl Crow Announces New Album, Pick You Up, Unveils “Freedom Bus” with Jesse Welles: Stream
items.summary:
Sheryl Crow has announced a new album called Pick You Up, due October 9 on Old Green Barn Productions, and released its closing track, "Freedom Bus," featuring Jesse Welles. The record runs seven songs, all of them written by Crow with Jeff Trott, her collaborator going back decades.

According to Consequence, a press release describes the album as a turn toward personal reflection and a return to the rock-leaning Americana singer-songwriter mode that defined Crow's 1990s run, with hope and unity as its recurring themes. It follows Evolution, her last studio album, released in 2024.

"Freedom Bus" leans on Crow's dry humor, opening with the lines "I guess today is Judgement Day/ Since everybody's got something to say." Welles joins on the chorus, harmonizing through "Whoever said freedom was free/ There ain't a freedom without history/ And folks who died for you and me/ So don't be an asshole, let every one be." It is a plain-spoken Americana song that never quite drops the grin.

The full tracklist opens with "Freight Train" and moves through "Perfect," the title track, "Flat Earth," "I've Got Your Number" and "Heaven Help Us" before closing on "Freedom Bus." Pre-orders are open now.

Crow, a nine-time Grammy winner and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, has live dates lined up around the release. She joins Willie Nelson's Outlaw Music Festival for stops in Wantagh, Bethel and Saratoga Springs, New York, from August 28 to 30, then opens two nights for Tedeschi Trucks Band at the Hartford HealthCare Amphitheater in Bridgeport, Connecticut, on September 4 and 5.

items.title: Read the Full Credits to Phoebe Bridgers’ Lost Weekend
items.summary:
Phoebe Bridgers has released Lost Weekend, her third solo album and her first since Punisher in 2020. The 16-track record includes lead single "Lost Boys" and marks her first proper solo material since the 2022 one-off "Sidelines."

Pitchfork published the album's full credits, and they run long. Bridgers produced the record with Tony Berg, Ethan Gruska, Jack Antonoff and Alex G, with writing contributions from Christian Lee Hutson, Marshall Vore, Bo Burnham, Lucy Dacus, Maya Hawke, Ethan Gruska, Alex G and Damien Jurado across various tracks.

The performer list is similarly crowded. Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus sing on multiple songs, Caroline Shaw appears throughout on vocals and viola, and Chris Thile, Greg Leisz, Rob Moose, Blake Mills, Nick Zinner, Jim Keltner, Sebastian Steinberg, Nickel Creek and Justin K Broadrick of Jesu all turn up in the instrument credits. Bridgers' brother Jackson contributes vocals, as does her pug, Maxine. The title track samples Paul Lansky's "Notjustmoreidlechatter."

The album arrived after an unusually elaborate rollout: pop-up shows, a phones-free charity performance at Madison Square Garden, and listening parties held at planetariums around the world.

Bridgers will tour behind Lost Weekend next year in North America and Europe. Alex G opens the North American dates; Isaac Wood, formerly of Black Country, New Road, supports in Europe.

items.title: Watch the Nicole Kidman-Led Music Video for Troye Sivan’s New Song
items.summary:
Troye Sivan has announced his fourth studio album, She's the Best, arriving October 9, and released its title track alongside a music video starring Nicole Kidman. The announcement caps a run of Instagram teasers Sivan had been posting for the record.

Pitchfork reported that the album follows a series of posts building toward both the LP and its first single, which shares the album's name. The video is Kidman's turn as the centerpiece of the song's visual, and it lands with the single rather than trailing behind it.

She's the Best is Sivan's first album since Something to Give Each Other in 2023, the record that produced "Rush" and "One of Your Girls." In 2024 he took the SWEAT tour to arenas as a co-headlining run with Charli XCX, a bill built around Something to Give Each Other and Brat.

With the title track and video out and an October release date set, Sivan's fourth album cycle is formally underway.

items.title: Troye Sivan announces new album She’s the Best
items.summary:
Troye Sivan has announced his fourth studio album, She's the Best, arriving October 9. He shared the news alongside confirmation that the title track, which he had been teasing for days, would land at midnight on August 14.

A music video accompanies the single. According to The FADER, a teaser indicates the clip is set in New York City and features a cast of glammed-up nightlife performers. The city looms over the whole rollout: Sivan spent the preceding week posting New York-set visual teasers and photos of himself with rockabilly-styled hair.

The album art, also released with the announcement, shows a woman in full cabaret glam, topless but for sparkly pasties, smoking a cigarette next to an overground New York subway line. It fits the aesthetic the teasers had been circling.

She's the Best is Sivan's first album since 2023's Something to Give Each Other, which earned three Grammy nominations and produced "Rush" and "One of Your Girls." After that record he hit the road with Charli xcx on their joint SWEAT Tour.

Pre-orders are live now, including signed vinyl and CDs, through Sivan's official store link.

items.title: ‘Black Mirror’ Director Ally Pankiw Roasts ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series, Claiming She Turned Down Gig: “Say No To Funding Transphobia”
items.summary:
Director Ally Pankiw has publicly declined an opportunity to work on HBO's forthcoming Harry Potter series, posting what appears to be a text exchange with her agent about the offer. "It is simply this easy to say no to funding transphobia," Pankiw wrote in the caption, adding that the opportunity was for directing, "not acting obviously lol."

In the screenshot, her agent writes, "I have an instinct on the answer but I feel compelled to ask. Harry Potter? Hard no?" Pankiw replies, "Absolutely fucking not! lol (But thank you for asking)." The agent responds, "Of course :) I assumed as much (And agree)."

Deadline reported the post and said it has reached out to HBO to confirm whether Pankiw was on the network's list of directors. Pankiw's credits include Black Mirror and The Great.

The post drew support from actor and comedian Vic Michaelis, actress Taylor Ortega and director Kate Herron, whose work includes Loki, Doctor Who and Sex Education. Herron commented that the series had approached her twice: "They've asked me twice and I've had to explain my answer is never going to change from a no."

The reaction reflects ongoing friction around J.K. Rowling, who created the books and serves as an executive producer on the series alongside Neil Blair, Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV and David Heyman of Heyday Films. Rowling's views on trans people have distanced her from film franchise stars Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint, and series cast members Nick Frost, John Lithgow, Paapa Essiedu and Bel Powley have openly disagreed with her while facing online criticism for taking the roles.

Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, named after the first film, premieres Christmas Day on HBO and streams exclusively on HBO Max worldwide.
